Goode and Doug Maclean came in together in third place and Davies and Hewson, the junior half-miler, of Mitcham, were next home. Johnny Godfrey and Pete Adams also ran well, as did H.
Casselton give us the lead, which was held by both Frank Kemp and Alan Law, but Gerry Trower could not match the strong finish of Hewson of Mitcham, and so we finished second in this event.
Wright beat Hewson of Mitcham in the half-mile, and this youngster is a champion of the future, while Geoff Goode met his match in Boyd of the home club in the 1 mile.

Casselton was third in the junior 440, and Gerry Trower ran the race of his life in the half-mile, only to lose to Hewson of Mitcham, who did 1 min. 56.7 secs., and Gerry was clocked at 1 min. 59.4 secs., which must be the fastest time ever recorded by a club junior member!
Wise ran really well to chase Brian Hewson home in the 880 yards, although the time was rather slow and Hewson seemed to be playing with the opposition.
Bob Taylor was also down as a reserve for the 880 yards, but here again the two first strings, Day and Hewson, turned out, so Bob was not called upon to run.

There is nothing unusual about the training of Iharos, Chataway, Zatopek, Pirie, Norris Hewson and the rest - these men are quite normal individuals - everyone can adopt the same technique but the work involved must be built up over a number of years.

From 1955 to the early 60's John's track career as a middle-distance runner fell only just so very, very short of full international status, but it should be noted that at that time he was vying with some of the great names of the past — Hewson, Chataway, Brasher and Pirie to name but a few.
